raw_response:
I will keep the full 6.0 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that fits my land, my well irrigation, and the labor my family can put in. I do not farm by guesswork now; I look at yield target, fertilizer cost, and how stable the crop is in our area. For wheat, I will stay a little heavier on nitrogen because I would rather spend a bit more than lose tillers and ears early. I will keep phosphorus steady for root growth and early vigor, and I will not cut potassium too low because the wheat-maize rotation removes a lot over the year. With well water, I will irrigate wheat three times if the weather is normal: once after sowing or at overwintering if moisture is short, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed and keep fertilizer strong enough to support a good ear, but I will not overspend on unnecessary passes since I only have 6 mu and some family labor is tied up off-farm. I will plant maize right after wheat harvest, mostly keep residue and use no-tillage or very light disturbance to save time and moisture. I will plan for two pesticide rounds on each crop in a normal year, then add only if pest pressure is obvious. My target is steady output, not chasing extreme yield with excessive cost.
